Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both wake visualizations. I’ll use the fish-control bookshelf at the required decision point, translating only a defensible invariant into the two-joint policy.

The `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill also applies here: it requires both moving-window views to be inspected before any controller change. I’ll let that visual evidence constrain the mechanism choice, and I’ll record the diagnosis before touching the candidate.

The scalar summaries hide an important tradeoff: the unguarded soft-envelope carrier is fastest (`16.943T`) but sits exactly on both joint-speed limits, while the parent’s phase-local guard removes all exact contacts and retains capture at `17.115T`. I’m now comparing that strong capture visually with the reallocation variant, which also stays speed-viable but regresses to `17.275T`.

The inherited logs make the next mechanism sharper. The prior reallocation sent guarded anterior acceleration toward the posterior carrier even though, at all 115 anterior-limit samples in the strong baseline, the posterior command was never simultaneously doing positive joint work. By contrast, 96 of 109 posterior-limit samples had safe, positive-work anterior activity. I’ll record and test that observed asymmetry, keeping the parent’s successful high-onset guard unchanged.

The candidate now adds one bounded mechanism: guarded posterior work can flow to the anterior oscillator only during an already positive-work phase and only with normalized speed/acceleration headroom. The existing steering, carrier, soft acceleration envelope, speed guard, and angle viability logic are unchanged. Next I’m distilling the completed opposite-direction result as a reusable negative lesson; I won’t treat this unevaluated candidate as evidence.

The first required check exposed a workspace-rendering issue rather than a content failure: `README.md` lists the same guidance parent twice as “prefill,” so the checker counts two parents. I’m inspecting the checker’s parent-selection logic and will repair only an allowed workspace file if possible; I won’t weaken the validation.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicate parent marker from the rendered workspace README. The Julia contract check itself has not run because this shell lacks `julia` on `PATH`; I’m locating the workspace/runtime binary, then I’ll run the remaining boundary and schema checks.

The boundary check passes, and a static schema comparison shows every `params.FIELD` reference is returned by `target_policy_params()`. Per the workspace contract, I’m now invoking the dedicated check-runner for an independent final audit; no CFD will be run.

The dedicated check-runner could not start because its configured `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported in this account. I’ve already executed its checks locally; I’m falling back to an independent default runner using the same TOML commands so the audit still completes.

A non-CFD replay caught an important design issue before handoff: capping the transfer at the existing soft ceiling would make it negligible (mean `0.003 rad/T²`). I’m tightening the design to use only the small, explicit `0.95→0.99` physical acceleration reserve. On the logged strong trace that yields 119 selective transfers, averaging `1.10` and peaking at `1.28 rad/T²`, while remaining below the hard envelope.

The independent re-audit passes the guidance, boundary, and 25-field schema checks. The only unavailable check is Julia execution because no Julia binary exists in this workspace environment; the candidate’s executable assertions therefore could not be run here. I’m doing one final file-integrity pass now.

Completed one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:223) adds phase-compatible posterior-to-anterior work reallocation with normalized speed and acceleration headroom.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, inherited evidence, replay, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:165) now captures the negative result that actuator headroom without positive-work phase compatibility is insufficient.

Validation:

- Guidance contract: PASS
- Solver boundary: PASS
- Parameter schema: PASS, 25/25 fields
- Exactly one nonempty candidate: PASS
- Julia runtime check: unavailable (`julia: command not found`)
- CFD was not run, as required

I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that prevented the mandated guidance checker from running.
